user_input: How do I reset my expired Active Directory password from the lock screen?
response: On the Windows lock screen click "I forgot my password", verify your identity with the Microsoft Authenticator push notification, then set a new password that is at least 12 characters with one uppercase, one number, and one symbol. The change syncs to all corporate apps within 15 minutes.
retrieved_contexts: Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR): From the Windows lock screen, click "I forgot my password" to launch the SSPR portal. Identity is verified through a Microsoft Authenticator push notification.

Corporate password policy: minimum 12 characters, must include at least one uppercase letter, one number, and one symbol. After a successful reset, the new password propagates to all integrated corporate apps within 15 minutes.
reference: From the lock screen click "I forgot my password", verify your identity with the Microsoft Authenticator push notification, then set a new password of at least 12 characters including one uppercase, one number, and one symbol. It syncs to all corporate apps within 15 minutes.

user_input: My Outlook keeps asking me to re-enter my password every few hours. How do I fix it?
response: This is usually a cached-credential issue. Open Control Panel > Credential Manager, remove the stored entries under "MicrosoftOffice16", then restart Outlook and sign in once with your full email address. If it persists, the contexts say to clear the Outlook profile in the Mail (Microsoft Outlook) control panel and create a new profile.
retrieved_contexts: Repeated Outlook credential prompts are most often caused by stale cached credentials. Resolution: open Control Panel > Credential Manager and delete the stored entries beginning with "MicrosoftOffice16", then restart Outlook and sign in with the full email address.
If the prompts continue after clearing Credential Manager, remove the corrupted Outlook profile via Control Panel > Mail (Microsoft Outlook) and create a new profile.
reference: Repeated Outlook password prompts are typically stale cached credentials: open Credential Manager, delete the "MicrosoftOffice16" entries, restart Outlook and sign in with your full email address. If it continues, delete the Outlook profile in Control Panel > Mail and create a new profile.

user_input: What is the SLA for a Priority 2 incident and who handles it?
response: A Priority 2 (P2) incident has a 30-minute response target and a 4-hour resolution target. It is handled by the Tier 2 service desk during business hours, and if it is still open after 4 hours it is automatically escalated to the Tier 3 infrastructure team.
retrieved_contexts: Incident SLA matrix: Priority 1 (P1) - 15-minute response, 2-hour resolution. Priority 2 (P2) - 30-minute response, 4-hour resolution. Priority 3 (P3) - 4-hour response, 2-business-day resolution.

Ownership and escalation: P2 incidents are owned by the Tier 2 service desk during business hours. Any P2 that remains open past its 4-hour resolution target is automatically escalated to the Tier 3 infrastructure team.
reference: A Priority 2 incident has a 30-minute response target and a 4-hour resolution target. It is owned by the Tier 2 service desk during business hours and is automatically escalated to the Tier 3 infrastructure team if it remains open past 4 hours.

user_input: How do I connect to internal systems when I'm working from home?
response: Use the GlobalProtect VPN client. Open GlobalProtect, enter the portal address vpn.corp.example.com, and sign in with your SSO credentials plus the Authenticator push approval. Once the status shows "Connected", internal systems on the 10.0.0.0/8 network become reachable. Split tunneling is enabled, so only corporate traffic is routed through the VPN.
retrieved_contexts: Remote access is provided through the GlobalProtect VPN client. Connect to the portal vpn.corp.example.com and authenticate with your single sign-on (SSO) credentials and a Microsoft Authenticator push approval.
Once GlobalProtect shows "Connected", systems on the internal 10.0.0.0/8 network are reachable. The VPN uses split tunneling, so only corporate-bound traffic is routed through the tunnel.
reference: Connect with the GlobalProtect VPN client to the portal vpn.corp.example.com using your SSO credentials and a Microsoft Authenticator push approval. When it shows "Connected", internal systems on the 10.0.0.0/8 network are reachable, and split tunneling routes only corporate traffic through the VPN.

user_input: How do I request a software install that isn't in the Company Portal?
response: Submit a Software Request ticket in the ServiceNow catalog under "Request Something > Software". Your manager must approve it, then the security team reviews the application against the approved-software list. Approved installs are pushed automatically through Intune within two business days; you don't need local admin rights.
retrieved_contexts: For software not available in the Company Portal, submit a Software Request through the ServiceNow catalog: Request Something > Software. The request requires manager approval followed by a security team review against the approved-software list.
Once approved, the application is deployed automatically via Microsoft Intune within two business days. Users do not need local administrator rights because installation is handled by Intune.
reference: Submit a Software Request in the ServiceNow catalog under Request Something > Software. It needs manager approval and a security review against the approved-software list, after which the app is deployed automatically through Microsoft Intune within two business days, with no local admin rights required.
